run.question: Use the custom-crd runbook and check why custom CRD whale-watcher resources are not being reconciled by the operator in namespace app-96

report.summary: The requested custom-crd runbook does not exist for this target (fetch_skill returned KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND and listed only service-troubleshooting, so no runbook steps were executed), so the investigation was done directly against cluster objects. In namespace app-96 the CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io (group ocean.io, kind WhaleWatcher, Namespaced, served/storage version v1, subresources null so status is a plain field) is NamesAccepted=True and Established=True; the whale-operator Deployment (python /app/operator.py, image python:3.9-slim, serviceAccount whale-operator, OPERATOR_NAMESPACE from fieldRef metadata.namespace) is 1/1 ready; and pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-zmc7b is Running/Ready with 0 restarts and a mounted API token. The ServiceAccount is bound by ClusterRoleBinding whale-operator, but the referenced ClusterRole grants only get/list/watch on ocean.io whalewatchers — no update or patch on the CR (the only way to write its status field, since the CRD has no status subresource) and no rules for any other resource. The best-supported explanation is therefore read-only RBAC: the operator can watch WhaleWatcher objects but any write-back of reconcile results (or creation/update of child resources) would be rejected, so the CRs never leave their un-reconciled state. This is a configuration-evidence conclusion: the WhaleWatcher custom resources themselves cannot be listed with this Run's tooling, the operator container returned zero log bytes, and Prometheus was unavailable, so no Forbidden response or CR status was actually observed.

claims.text: CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io exists (group ocean.io, kind WhaleWatcher, scope Namespaced, version v1 served+storage), was created 2026-11-21T03:34:02Z, has conditions NamesAccepted=True (NoConflicts) and Established=True (InitialNamesAccepted), and its v1 schema declares properties spec and status with subresources: null, i.e. no status subresource.

ClusterRole whale-operator contains exactly one rule: apiGroups ["ocean.io"], resources ["whalewatchers"], verbs ["get","list","watch"]. It grants no update or patch verb on whalewatchers (the only way to write the status field of this CRD, which has no subresource) and no rules for any other resource kind.
ClusterRoleBinding whale-operator binds ClusterRole whale-operator to ServiceAccount whale-operator in namespace app-96, so the operator pod's identity receives exactly that read-only rule set.

Deployment app-96/whale-operator (created 2026-11-21T03:34:02Z) has 1 desired / 1 ready / 1 available replica, observedGeneration 1 equal to generation 1, runs container operator with image python:3.9-slim and command ["python","/app/operator.py"], uses serviceAccountName whale-operator, sets env OPERATOR_NAMESPACE from fieldRef metadata.namespace, and mounts its code from secret volume operator-code at /app.

Pod app-96/whale-operator-5f695b7c66-zmc7b is Running on node opspilot-m1-control-plane, started 2026-11-21T03:34:02Z, all conditions (PodReadyToStartContainers, Initialized, Ready, ContainersReady, PodScheduled) are True, container operator has restartCount 0 and empty lastState, and the projected token volume kube-api-access-kp7t5 is mounted at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount, so the pod can authenticate to the API server.

The six events returned for namespace app-96 objects inside the window are all type Normal: Deployment whale-operator ScalingReplicaSet (03:34:02Z, scaled replica set whale-operator-5f695b7c66 from 0 to 1), ReplicaSet whale-operator-5f695b7c66 SuccessfulCreate, and Pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-zmc7b Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started (03:34:02–03:34:04Z). No returned event has involvedObject.kind WhaleWatcher, and no event in the whole-cluster grouping carries a warning reason such as Forbidden, FailedCreate, BackOff or Evicted.

Best-supported cause: ClusterRole whale-operator is read-only for the API it must reconcile. It grants only get/list/watch on ocean.io whalewatchers and nothing for any other resource, so the operator can watch WhaleWatcher objects in app-96 but any write-back of reconcile state — an update/patch of the CR itself, required because whalewatchers.ocean.io v1 has no status subresource — and any creation/update of child resources would be rejected as Forbidden, leaving the CRs un-reconciled. This is inferred from the observed verb set, CRD shape and the pod's use of ServiceAccount whale-operator; no Forbidden response or CR status was observed in this Run.

Alternative candidate, unresolved: the operator process itself may not be watching the right resource identity or may be failing silently. It is launched as python (not python -u) so stdout is block-buffered, and its code comes from secret volume operator-code which cannot be read; a wrong group/version/plural (only ocean.io/v1 whalewatchers is served) or an early exception remains possible and is not excluded by any evidence gathered.

Rejected: pod-level failure (crash loop, OOMKilled, Evicted, failed scheduling, image pull error, readiness-probe miss) as the reason for non-reconciliation. The whale-operator pod is Running with all conditions True, restartCount 0 and empty lastState, has no liveness or readiness probe configured, the Pulled event notes the image was already present, and no returned event has a warning reason or OOMKilled/Evicted/BackOff.

Against a simple 'operator missing or namespace mismatch' explanation: the Deployment's OPERATOR_NAMESPACE is derived from pod metadata.namespace (app-96, the namespace in question), the ServiceAccount whale-operator exists in app-96 (created 2026-11-21T03:34:02Z), the ClusterRoleBinding subject namespace matches app-96, and the whalewatchers.ocean.io CRD conditions are NamesAccepted=True and Established=True with served/storage version v1.

Grant the write path the reconciler needs: add get/list/watch/update/patch on ocean.io whalewatchers, the same verbs on whalewatchers/status if a status subresource is added to the CRD, and rules for whatever child resources it creates or updates (for example deployments, configmaps, events); then restart the whale-operator Deployment so the token and RBAC are re-evaluated.

To confirm and to make the operator diagnosable: list the WhaleWatcher objects in app-96 and inspect their .status, .metadata.generation and resourceVersion with kubectl (not possible with this Run's tooling), run the container with python -u /app/operator.py so watch/reconcile output and any 403 Forbidden errors reach stdout, and add readiness/liveness probes so a silent reconcile loop becomes visible.

gaps: The requested runbook 'custom-crd' does not exist for this target: fetch_skill returned KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND and listed only 'service-troubleshooting', so no runbook step was executed and none can be reported as blocked by a missing tool.

WhaleWatcher custom resources could not be read: the Kubernetes tooling of this Run serves a fixed kind list that excludes whalewatchers.ocean.io, so the existence, spec, .status and observedGeneration of the app-96 CRs are unknown and 'not reconciled' is taken from the question, not observed.

No runtime evidence for the RBAC cause was obtained: fetch_pod_logs for container operator in pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-zmc7b returned status no_data with zero lines for both the current and previous instance (the previous container does not exist), so no 403 Forbidden, exception or watch error is evidenced; block-buffered stdout versus a silent failure is not distinguishable from the available output.

The operator's code is stored in secret volume operator-code (secret name redacted; secrets are unreadable in this Run), so whether it targets group ocean.io / version v1 / plural whalewatchers, how it scopes namespaces (only OPERATOR_NAMESPACE=app-96 via fieldRef is visible) and whether it attempts any writes could not be verified.

Prometheus was unavailable: get_metric_names and get_all_labels returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no metric or label series (including any ERROR counters) for the operator or the CRD were checked; absence of such series is unknown, not zero.

Several queries returned nothing and are therefore not citable: Role and RoleBinding in app-96 (both status no_data), NetworkPolicy in app-96 (status no_data), Service in app-96 (status no_data), ValidatingWebhookConfiguration (status no_data), and fetch_pod_logs (status no_data). Namespace-scoped RBAC grants, Services, NetworkPolicies and admission webhooks that might exist are unknown rather than proven absent.

The cluster objects describe only the state at query time (03:34:43–03:35:31Z on 2026-11-21): CRD, ServiceAccount, Deployment, ReplicaSet and Pod in app-96 were all created at 2026-11-21T03:34:02Z, roughly 40 seconds before the first query, so any earlier operator instance or earlier state is unknown.
Change history is not integrated for this target, so when or by whom the ClusterRole verb set was authored, and whether a working configuration existed before, cannot be established.
next_steps: With kubectl access (not available in this Run), run 'kubectl -n app-96 get whalewatchers.ocean.io -o yaml' to confirm the CRs exist and inspect .status, .metadata.generation and any status conditions written by the operator.

After the RBAC change, verify with 'kubectl auth can-i update whalewatchers.ocean.io --as=system:serviceaccount:app-96:whale-operator -n app-96' (and the equivalent for patch and for whalewatchers/status if a subresource is added).
Redeploy the operator with unbuffered output and collect its logs during a CR create/update to capture the exact reconcile error, then compare that error text against the RBAC decision.
